The search turned up Cloudflare's guide for connecting an Agent to an MCP server, but no page that walks through the raw `initialize` request itself.

**Connecting from an Agent:** The Cloudflare tutorial starts from the hello-world template and adds an endpoint that handles connection requests. In that example, a POST handler reads a server URL and name from the request body and calls `addMcpServer()` to open the connection. Per the docs, if the server requires OAuth, the response includes an `authUrl` that the user must visit to finish authorization.

**Where the initialize handshake shows up:** The agents package release notes mention it. One release explains that agents can respond to server-initiated `elicitation/create` requests by calling `this.mcp.configureElicitationHandlers({ form, url })`, typically in `onStart()`. The same notes say that connections advertise elicitation modes at the initialize handshake, and without handlers they advertise no elicitation capability. So the capabilities the client sends during initialize depend on the handlers you configure. I couldn't find the exact initialize payload format in these results. The SDK source or the MCP specification would be the place to confirm it.

**Transport choice:** Cloudflare's transport page says RPC transport doesn't support authentication, so use Streamable HTTP for external connections that require OAuth.

**Testing:** To check a server you've built, the docs suggest the MCP Inspector, which is an interactive MCP client that lets you connect to your MCP server and invoke tools from a web browser.

If you want the wire-level details of the initialize request, I can run a narrower search on the agents SDK source or the MCP specification.

content.text:
The Cloudflare Agents MCP client follows the standard MCP lifecycle, so the first thing it sends is a JSON-RPC **`initialize` request**. That request carries the client's protocol version, client info and capabilities. The server replies with its own capabilities, then the client sends a `notifications/initialized` notification. Only after that does it make normal calls like `tools/list`.

The Cloudflare release notes confirm that the capabilities sent at this handshake depend on your setup. If you call `this.mcp.configureElicitationHandlers()`, the client advertises elicitation support. If you don't, it advertises none.

One caveat: Cloudflare's docs don't show the exact wire payload. The "initialize first" order comes from the MCP specification, which the Agents SDK implements. Also, if the server needs OAuth, `addMcpServer()` returns an `authUrl`, and the handshake can't finish until the user completes authorization.

Sources:
- [Connect to an MCP server – Cloudflare Docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/guides/connect-mcp-client)
- [connect mcp client – Cloudflare Docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/model-context-protocol/guides/connect-mcp-client/)
- [cloudflare/agents agents@0.17.4 release notes](https://newreleases.io/project/github/cloudflare/agents/release/agents@0.17.4)
- [MCP transport – Cloudflare Docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/model-context-protocol/transport/)
